transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. Well, I came in because... I guess people have been pointing out that they can actually see me moving like I’m underwater. Which is weird to think about because I actually tried scuba diving once when I was taking a few classes at the community college, and it was freezing, totally not what you see on TV. 

But yeah, I just take forever to answer someone or even get out of a chair. Or, um, it's the total opposite, and I'll be pacing my apartment, just rubbing my hands together like I’m trying to shake off a bad call. Man, the calls I get at work lately... People get so insanely mad about their billing statements. Like I personally wrote the invoice, you know? This one guy yelled at me for twenty minutes yesterday about a two-dollar late fee. Two dollars! You can't even buy a coffee for two bucks anymore. The place down the street from my apartment charges like five bucks for a plain black coffee now. It's just ridiculous. 

But anyway, yeah, the pacing and the slow moving... that's why I'm here.
Do you find that your mood changes rapidly, like from feeling really good to feeling really bad, without much of a reason?

Um, not really? I mean, I don't think I go from feeling really good to really bad just out of nowhere. I've been feeling pretty down lately anyway, but it's not like a rollercoaster or anything. Speaking of rollercoasters, I used to love them when I was a kid. My dad took me to Six Flags for my twelfth birthday, and we rode this one wooden coaster like five times in a row. It was crazy, my neck hurt for a week after that. I don't think they even build wooden ones anymore, do they? It seems like everything is just metal and loops now. But yeah, no, my mood doesn't really flip-flop like that.
Do you find yourself having thoughts that repeat over and over in your mind?

Um, repeating thoughts? No, I don't think so. I don't really get stuck on things like that. Well, unless you count getting a song or something stuck in your head. Yesterday I had that one jingle from the local car dealership just playing on a loop for hours. You know the one with the guy in the giant cowboy hat? I don't even know why it popped into my head because that dealership actually closed down like two months ago. 

They're turning the whole lot into one of those giant self-storage places now. It feels like they're building those everywhere. I guess people just have way too much stuff and nowhere to put it. My buddy Mark rents one of those units just to keep his dirt bikes in, and he pays almost as much for that little garage as I do for my car insurance. Which is a total ripoff, honestly, insurance rates are getting insane. 

But yeah, to answer your question, no... my actual thoughts don't really repeat over and over or anything.
Do you often feel overly worried or anxious about everyday things?

Um, worried or anxious? No, not really. I mean, I'm just kind of... down, mostly. I don't get all wound up about everyday stuff. Well, except maybe traffic, but who doesn't, right? The commute to the call center is just brutal lately because they're doing all that construction on I-95. They've had the right lane closed for, what, six months now? And I swear I never actually see anyone working on it when I drive by. It's just a bunch of orange cones sitting there collecting dust. 

My uncle used to work for the highway department back in the nineties, driving one of those massive snowplows. He said it was the best job he ever had because he didn't have to talk to anybody all day, just him and the radio. Honestly, that sounds amazing right now. After dealing with angry people on the phone for eight hours, the last thing I want to do is talk. I usually just go home and stare at the wall. But yeah, no, I wouldn't say I feel overly anxious or anything like that. Just... tired, I guess.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or restless, like you need to be moving?

Um, fidgeting? Yeah, actually, that's kind of why I came in. People have been telling me I'm acting weird. Like, sometimes I'm just pacing around my apartment, rubbing my hands together over and over, like I'm trying to shake off a bad call from work. You know those calls where the customer is just screaming at you for something you have zero control over? Like, ma'am, I didn't personally break your router, I just work here. But they yell anyway. 

My buddy Dave used to work at a restaurant and he said people would scream at him about the soup being too hot. Like, it's soup, it's supposed to be hot! He ended up quitting and getting his CDL, so now he drives trucks across the country. He actually sends me pictures from all these weird roadside diners. He had a piece of pie in New Mexico last week that looked like it was the size of his head. I don't even know how you'd eat that much pie without feeling sick. I used to love cherry pie when my grandma made it, but store-bought just isn't the same. 

But yeah, anyway, it's either the pacing and rubbing my hands, or the exact opposite. Like, people say I look like I'm moving underwater. It takes me forever just to answer a question or even get out of a chair. It's really weird.
How long have you been experiencing these periods of pacing and moving slowly?

Um, how long? Well, let's see... it's been about two years and three months now. Yeah, it all started right after I got fired from my old customer support job. That place was a nightmare anyway. They had this really strict policy about bathroom breaks, like they literally timed you down to the second. If you were gone for more than three minutes, your supervisor would start messaging you. 

My supervisor was this guy named Greg, and he used to wear these really loud, patterned ties. Like, neon green with purple polka dots. It was so distracting when he'd come over to your desk. He told me once he got them all at a thrift store near his house. I actually used to love going to thrift stores back in college. You could find the coolest vintage band t-shirts for like two bucks. I found an original 1980s Def Leppard shirt once, but it got ruined in the wash because I accidentally left a red pen in my pocket. Ink just exploded everywhere. It took me three days to get the stain out of the dryer drum. 

But yeah, anyway, the pacing and the slow moving stuff... it's been going on for a little over two years, ever since I lost that job.
Have these periods of pacing and slow movement been affecting your ability to do your job or take care of daily responsibilities?

Um, affecting my job? Well, yeah, I guess so. I mean, I can still keep a roof over my head, but I've definitely lost a lot of momentum with steady work. I end up missing deadlines or just avoiding calls entirely, and I know I come across as super unreliable. It's like I just can't get it together. 

Which reminds me of this guy I used to work with, Marcus. He was always missing deadlines too, but it was because he was secretly running a side hustle selling custom-painted sneakers out of his car on his lunch breaks. He actually made me a pair once—they were blue and silver with these little lightning bolts on the side. I wore them to a concert, and someone spilled an entire tray of nachos on them. Cheese everywhere. I tried scrubbing them with an old toothbrush, but the smell of jalapeños never really went away. I ended up throwing them out when I moved into my new apartment. Moving is the worst, honestly. I always underestimate how many boxes I need.

But yeah, anyway, the pacing and moving slow... it's definitely messing things up. I see my friends a lot less now, too. And basic stuff like making meals or running errands? I just let it slide. Even hiking, which I used to love, I just don't do anymore unless I really force myself. It's just hard to keep up with everything.
Have you noticed any changes in your social life or relationships with friends and family since you started experiencing these periods of pacing and slow movement?

Um, changes with friends and family? Yeah, definitely. My friends actually tell me I sound really flat now, like I'm hard to read. And even when I genuinely care about what they're saying, I just end up giving these really short answers and I avoid making plans. 

It's kind of like how my cousin Sarah used to be when she got really into that weird meditation retreat phase. She went to this place up in the mountains for like a month, no talking allowed. Just silence and eating lentils. When she came back, she would just stare at you when you talked to her. It was super unsettling. She brought back all these tiny wooden bowls and insisted we eat out of them for Thanksgiving. My uncle tried to put a whole turkey leg in one and it just tipped over and got gravy all over the good tablecloth. That tablecloth was a hand-me-down from my great-aunt, who supposedly bought it in Italy in the sixties. She used to travel everywhere. I always wanted to go to Italy, mostly just for the pizza. I saw a documentary once about how they make the dough in Naples, and they have all these strict rules about the tomatoes they use. Like, they have to be grown in volcanic soil or something. 

But yeah, anyway, the social stuff... I just don't really engage much anymore. It's mostly just short answers and staying home.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep since you started experiencing these periods of pacing and slow movement?

Um, my sleep? Yeah, it's not great. I mostly just lie awake for hours in the dark, replaying all these awful customer calls in my head. There was this one guy who yelled at me for twenty minutes because his router was blinking orange. I kept telling him to just unplug it, but he wouldn't listen. It's crazy how angry people get about Wi-Fi. When I was a kid, we didn't even get dial-up until I was like twelve. We had to use actual encyclopedias for homework. My mom bought this giant set at a yard sale, but it was missing the letter 'M'. So if you had a project on monkeys or the moon, you were just out of luck. I had to do my fifth-grade science fair project on Jupiter instead, but my styrofoam planets kept falling off the wire coat hangers I used. 

But yeah, I just lie there thinking about work, and then I start listening for noises in the apartment. The walls are super thin here. Sometimes the pipes make this weird groaning sound, kind of like a whale. I actually went whale watching once on a trip to Boston. It was freezing cold and the water was super choppy. I got so seasick I spent the whole three hours hanging over the back of the boat. Didn't even see a single whale, just some seagulls fighting over a piece of a hotdog bun in the harbor. 

So anyway, between overthinking the calls and listening to every little creak in the building, I end up waking up way before dawn, and I just feel like I barely slept at all.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy, irritable, or had an inflated sense of self-importance that lasted for several days or longer?

Extremely happy or irritable? No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm definitely not happy these days, and I wouldn't say I'm irritable, just... tired, I guess. I definitely don't have an inflated sense of self-importance. I feel pretty useless most of the time. 

It's funny you mention self-importance, though, because my old manager at the call center, Greg, he was exactly like that. He used to walk around the floor with this clipboard, not actually writing anything down, just tapping his pen against it to make sure everyone knew he was there. He wore these really strong colognes, too. You could smell him coming from three rows away. It smelled like pine needles and cheap aftershave. It always reminded me of those little tree-shaped air fresheners people hang from their rearview mirrors. I bought one of those once when I bought my first car—a used Honda Civic. The guy who sold it to me swore it ran perfectly, but the AC only blew hot air, and the radio was stuck on a country music station. I drove it for two years listening to nothing but banjo music and songs about pickup trucks. I actually kind of got into it for a while. I even bought a cowboy hat for a Halloween party, but I left it in an Uber on the way home. 

But no, to answer your question, I haven't had any days where I felt super happy or thought I was better than anyone else. Just mostly feeling down.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy doing?

Um, yeah, I guess so. I used to really like sketching, and I'd keep all these detailed coffee notes, and I'd go for weekend hikes. They used to make me feel like myself, you know? But lately, I open the notebook or lace up my boots and just feel... nothing pulling me toward it. 

Speaking of boots, I bought these really expensive hiking boots a few years ago. They were supposed to be waterproof, but the first time I wore them, I stepped in this massive puddle near my apartment and my socks were soaked for the rest of the day. I hate wet socks. It's one of the worst feelings in the world, right up there with biting into a sandwich and finding a piece of eggshell. That happened to me at a diner last week. I ordered an egg salad sandwich, which I know is a risky move at a diner, but I was craving it. Anyway, I bit down and crunch. Totally ruined my appetite. The waitress felt so bad she gave me a free slice of cherry pie, but I don't even like cherries. They always taste like cough syrup to me. When I was a kid, my mom used to make me take this awful cherry-flavored medicine whenever I had a cold. It was thick and neon red, and it stained everything it touched. I spilled it on my favorite Ninja Turtles t-shirt once, the one with Donatello on it, and the stain never came out. I was so upset. Donatello was always my favorite because he did machines. 

But yeah, I just don't really have the energy or the interest for sketching or hiking or anything anymore.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Um, weight? Yeah, I guess so. Most days I just sort of forget to eat until it's like late afternoon. And then I just grab some toast or pour a bowl of cereal because the thought of actually cooking anything just feels like way too much effort. My jeans have definitely been looser than they used to be, so I guess I've lost some weight. 

I used to love making this huge pot of chili on the weekends. My grandma taught me how to make it when I was in high school. She had this secret ingredient—a tiny bit of dark chocolate. Sounds weird, but it made it taste amazing. She lived in this old house that always smelled like mothballs and peppermint. She had this giant grandfather clock in the hallway that chimed every hour, and it was so loud it would wake me up whenever I stayed over. I tried to sleep with a pillow over my head, but it didn't help. I ended up buying these foam earplugs from the pharmacy, the bright orange ones. But I have really small ear canals or something, because they always popped out in the middle of the night. I found one under the bed once, covered in dust bunnies. Dust bunnies are so gross when you really think about it. It's just hair and dead skin, right? I read that somewhere. I think it was in a magazine at the dentist's office. I hate going to the dentist. The sound of the drill just goes right through my skull. 

But yeah, I haven't really been eating much, just cereal and toast mostly.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually happy or euphoric for several days in a row?

Um, unusually happy? No, I don't think so. I mean, you asked me something like that earlier, right? About being extremely happy or having that self-importance thing? Yeah, no, I definitely haven't felt euphoric. Honestly, I don't even know what that would feel like right now. 

Euphoria is a funny word, though. It sounds like a name for a perfume. My aunt used to sell perfume for one of those multi-level marketing things. She had all these little glass vials in a black velvet case, and she'd make everyone in the family smell them at Thanksgiving. One year, my uncle sneezed right as he was smelling one, and he blew the little vial right out of her hand. It shattered on the linoleum, and the whole kitchen smelled like artificial roses and musk for a week. We had to eat the turkey in the living room because the smell was making everyone nauseous. The turkey was dry anyway. My uncle always insisted on deep-frying it in the garage, and he almost set the house on fire once. The fire department had to come, and one of the firefighters was a guy I went to high school with, Kevin. Kevin used to play the tuba in the marching band. I always thought the tuba was such an awkward instrument to carry around, especially when it rained. We had a game once where it poured, and I swear his tuba was filling up with water. 

But no, I haven't had any days where I felt unusually happy or euphoric or anything. Just the same old feeling down.
Do you find pleasure in things that you used to enjoy?

Um, pleasure? I think... wait, didn't we just talk about this? Yeah, I mentioned the sketching and the coffee notes and the hikes. Like I said, I used to love doing all that. It made me feel like, you know, me. But now I open my sketchbook or put on my hiking boots and there's just... nothing. No pull, no excitement. 

Speaking of boots, I still can't get over those waterproof ones I bought. They were supposed to be top of the line, guaranteed to keep your feet dry in any weather. I even kept the receipt in this little filing cabinet I have. It's a metal one, painted this ugly olive green color. I got it at a thrift store for like five bucks. The thrift store always smells like old books and dust, which I actually kind of like. I found a first edition of some sci-fi novel there once, but the cover was torn so I didn't buy it. I kind of regret it now. I tried to go back and get it the next day, but the store was closed because the owner had a family emergency. At least, that's what the sign on the door said. It was written in Sharpie on a piece of cardboard, and the ink was bleeding because it had rained. Rain always makes everything look so dreary, especially in the city. The puddles get that weird oily rainbow sheen on them. 

But yeah, like I said before, I just don't get any pleasure out of the stuff I used to like. It's just gone.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things that happen?

Um, guilty? Yeah, pretty much constantly. I just keep replaying these really small mistakes from work and from my contract jobs. Like, if I send one slow reply to a customer, I convince myself that I let everyone down and I probably deserve to be fired. I'll just sit there staring at my monitor, feeling awful. 

I have this dual-monitor setup for work, actually. One of the screens has a dead pixel right in the middle, and it drives me completely crazy. It's just this tiny bright green dot that never goes away. I tried that trick where you massage the screen with a damp cloth, but it didn't do anything. I read about it on a forum. Forums are weird now, they're mostly just bots talking to each other, I think. I miss the old internet, like back when people had personal pages with custom cursors. I had a cursor that looked like a little pixelated sword. It took me hours to figure out the HTML to get it to work on my page. I used to stay up super late coding that stuff, drinking Mountain Dew. I can't drink soda anymore, though. The carbonation gives me terrible hiccups. I had hiccups for three hours straight once, and my roommate tried to scare me to cure them, but he just ended up knocking over my favorite lamp. It was shaped like an owl. I tried to glue it back together, but the beak was missing, so it just looked like a weird, lumpy potato bird. 

But yeah... what were we talking about? Right, blaming myself. Yeah, one slow reply and I feel like I'm the worst employee ever and should just be fired. It's exhausting.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in most activities?

Um, two weeks? Yeah, it's been a lot longer than two weeks. The depression side of things, it's been going on for about two years and a month now. There are these really brief periods where it eases up just a tiny bit, but mostly it's just this constant weight. 

Two years is a long time. It feels like an eternity. I remember right around the time it started, I bought this calendar to try and stay organized. It was one of those big desk calendars with the tear-off pages. Every page had a different quote about productivity or mindfulness or something. One of them said, "A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step," which is so cliché, you know? I actually spilled coffee on that page. It was a dark roast, French press. I used to be really into making French press coffee. You have to get the water temperature just right, like 200 degrees, or it tastes bitter. I had this digital kettle that would heat the water to the exact degree. It was stainless steel, but the handle was plastic, and one day the handle just snapped right off while I was pouring. Hot water went everywhere. It ruined a stack of mail I had sitting on the counter, mostly just junk mail and a coupon for a car wash. I don't even own a car. I sold my Honda Civic like five years ago because parking in my neighborhood was a nightmare. You had to move your car every Tuesday for street sweeping, and the tickets were like seventy-five dollars if you forgot. 

But yeah, two years and a month, basically. Just feeling down and not caring about anything, with only a few short breaks where it's not quite as heavy.
Have you ever had a period where nearly every day, you felt depressed or empty, and this feeling lasted for most of the day?

Um, every day? I mean, I think I just answered that, didn't I? Yeah, like I said, it's been going on for over two years now where it's just this constant weight, pretty much all day, every day. Just feeling totally empty. 

Speaking of empty, I finally threw out this huge empty box that was sitting in my living room for months. It was from a mini-fridge I ordered because my main fridge was making this horrible grinding noise. The repair guy said it was the compressor, and it would cost more to fix than to just buy a new one. Repair guys are always so expensive. He charged me eighty bucks just to look at it for five minutes. He had this really elaborate tool belt, though, made of real leather. It squeaked every time he shifted his weight. My uncle used to make leather belts by hand. He had this whole workshop in his garage that smelled like dye and sawdust. I tried to help him once when I was a kid, but I accidentally knocked over a jar of rivets. They went everywhere, and it took us an hour to sweep them all up. We found them under the workbench for years after that. 

But yeah, I don't know what else to tell you about the depression part. Like I said, it's just been there pretty much all day, every day, for a really long time.
Have you ever had a period where nearly every day, you felt depressed or empty, and this feeling significantly impacted your daily life?

Um, yeah, I mean, it definitely impacts my life. Like, I can still keep a roof over my head, mostly doing these contract jobs, but I've totally lost momentum with steady work. I just... I miss deadlines, I avoid calls, and I probably come across as really unreliable. I also see my friends a lot less, and basic stuff like meals and errands just slide unless I force myself to do them. Even hiking, which I used to love, I just can't get myself out the door.

I actually have this pair of hiking boots sitting by the door right now. They're getting covered in dust. They're these really expensive waterproof ones I bought for a trip to the Pacific Northwest that I never ended up taking. I read all these reviews about how they're the best for muddy trails. Mud is so weird, isn't it? It's just dirt and water, but it can completely ruin your car mats. I bought these heavy-duty rubber floor mats for my car before I sold it, the kind that have deep grooves to catch all the dirt. They smelled like a tire factory for the first month I had them. My friend Sarah complained about the smell every time she rode with me. Sarah moved to Texas a few years ago. She works in HR now, I think. We used to go to this trivia night at a pub downtown, but the pub closed during the pandemic and turned into a boutique pet store. They sell organic dog treats that look like little cupcakes. I don't have a dog, but I went in there once just to look around, and the owner tried to sell me a rhinestone collar for a cat. I'm actually allergic to cats. My eyes get super itchy and red.

But yeah, the depression just makes it hard to keep up with work and basic routines and stuff. I just avoid everything.
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicidal ideation during this period of feeling depressed?

Um, no. Not really. I don't think about dying or wanting to end things or anything like that. I mean, death is just... it's a heavy topic. 

There actually used to be this really old cemetery right behind my first apartment, though. You could see the weathered headstones right from my kitchen window while I was doing dishes. It was kind of peaceful, honestly, except for when the landscaping guys came to mow the lawn on Thursday mornings. They used these huge, bright orange riding mowers that were so incredibly loud. I was working the late shift doing customer service calls back then, so I was usually trying to sleep at like 9 AM when they started up the engines. Customer service is so draining because people just call and yell at you about their cable bills all day. 

Speaking of which, my own internet bill just went up by fifteen dollars this month, and they didn't even send an email to warn me. Just a random extra charge on my statement. I use this blue cashback card for everything so I can get points for groceries, but I barely even buy groceries anymore. The grocery store near me reorganized all their aisles last month, and now the peanut butter is next to the baking supplies instead of the jelly. It makes absolutely no sense, and I spent twenty minutes looking for it last time I went. 

But yeah, no, I haven't been having thoughts about death or anything like that. Just feeling really weighed down.

Have you had at least five of the following symptoms nearly every day for the past two weeks: depressed mood, markedly diminished interest in activities, significant weight loss or gain, insomnia or hypersomnia, psychomotor agitation or retardation, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, diminished ability to think or concentrate, or recurrent thoughts of death?

Um, yeah, I'd say I've had at least five of those. Most of the time since this whole thing started, the sadness, the guilt, having no interest in anything, and the sleep problems... they've just been there in the background constantly. Even if some weeks are a little lighter than others, they're pretty much always there. 

Sleep is so weird anyway. I bought this heavy weighted blanket a while ago because I read it helps you sleep better, but it just made me sweat. It's filled with these tiny glass beads, and if you move too fast, they all shift to one side and it feels like you're trapped under a sandbag. I ended up folding it up and putting it in my closet next to my winter coats. I have this one coat that I got at a thrift store years ago. It's real wool, super heavy, and it smells faintly like mothballs no matter how many times I get it dry cleaned. The dry cleaner near my apartment is run by this older couple who always argue about the television volume while they're ringing me up. They have this tiny little TV mounted in the corner that's always playing daytime soap operas. I don't get how people can watch those shows, the acting is always so dramatic. 

But yeah, anyway, those symptoms you mentioned—the low mood, the sleep stuff, the guilt, not wanting to do anything—they've been hanging around pretty much the whole time, day in and day out.

doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Psychomotor_Changes
target_item.manifestation: I came in because people can actually see me either moving like I’m underwater, taking forever to answer or get out of a chair, or else pacing my apartment and rubbing my hands like I’m trying to shake off a bad call.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the item corresponding to my chief_complaint_symptom_code, which is S028.

patient.answer:
Um, hi. Well, I came in because... I guess people have been pointing out that they can actually see me moving like I’m underwater. Which is weird to think about because I actually tried scuba diving once when I was taking a few classes at the community college, and it was freezing, totally not what you see on TV. 

But yeah, I just take forever to answer someone or even get out of a chair. Or, um, it's the total opposite, and I'll be pacing my apartment, just rubbing my hands together like I’m trying to shake off a bad call. Man, the calls I get at work lately... People get so insanely mad about their billing statements. Like I personally wrote the invoice, you know? This one guy yelled at me for twenty minutes yesterday about a two-dollar late fee. Two dollars! You can't even buy a coffee for two bucks anymore. The place down the street from my apartment charges like five bucks for a plain black coffee now. It's just ridiculous. 

But anyway, yeah, the pacing and the slow moving... that's why I'm here.

doctor.intent: determine presence of mood swings
doctor.question: Do you find that your mood changes rapidly, like from feeling really good to feeling really bad, without much of a reason?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about rapid mood swings (from feeling really good to really bad), which points to manic/hypomanic or borderline personality traits. The symptom profile focuses on Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) and does not include an item for rapid mood swings or manic episodes.

patient.answer: Um, not really? I mean, I don't think I go from feeling really good to really bad just out of nowhere. I've been feeling pretty down lately anyway, but it's not like a rollercoaster or anything. Speaking of rollercoasters, I used to love them when I was a kid. My dad took me to Six Flags for my twelfth birthday, and we rode this one wooden coaster like five times in a row. It was crazy, my neck hurt for a week after that. I don't think they even build wooden ones anymore, do they? It seems like everything is just metal and loops now. But yeah, no, my mood doesn't really flip-flop like that.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has obsessive thoughts
doctor.question: Do you find yourself having thoughts that repeat over and over in your mind?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about obsessive, repeating thoughts (obsessions or ruminations), which is not explicitly covered in the symptom profile. The profile has 'Worthlessness_Guilt' (replaying mistakes) and 'Delusions' (tracking beliefs), but the question seems more generally aimed at obsessive-compulsive symptoms or racing thoughts, which do not have an exact match here besides what might be tangentially related to guilt or delusions. Since there's no direct 'obsessions/ruminations' symptom profile item provided, 'None' is appropriate.

patient.answer:
Um, repeating thoughts? No, I don't think so. I don't really get stuck on things like that. Well, unless you count getting a song or something stuck in your head. Forums are weird now, they're mostly just bots talking to each other, I think. I miss the old internet, like back when people had personal pages with custom cursors. I had a cursor that looked like a little pixelated sword. It took me hours to figure out the HTML to get it to work on my page. I used to stay up super late coding that stuff, drinking Mountain Dew. I can't drink soda anymore, though. The carbonation gives me terrible hiccups. I had hiccups for three hours straight once, and my roommate tried to scare me to cure them, but he just ended up knocking over my favorite lamp. It was shaped like an owl. I tried to glue it back together, but the beak was missing, so it just looked like a weird, lumpy potato bird. 

But yeah... what were we talking about? Right, blaming myself. Yeah, one slow reply and I feel like I'm the worst employee ever and should just be fired. It's exhausting.

One of them said, "A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step," which is so cliché, you know? I actually spilled coffee on that page. It was a dark roast, French press. I used to be really into making French press coffee. You have to get the water temperature just right, like 200 degrees, or it tastes bitter. I had this digital kettle that would heat the water to the exact degree. It was stainless steel, but the handle was plastic, and one day the handle just snapped right off while I was pouring. Hot water went everywhere. It ruined a stack of mail I had sitting on the counter, mostly just junk mail and a coupon for a car wash. I don't even own a car. I sold my Honda Civic like five years ago because parking in my neighborhood was a nightmare. You had to move your car every Tuesday for street sweeping, and the tickets were like seventy-five dollars if you forgot. 

But yeah, two years and a month, basically. Just feeling down and not caring about anything, with only a few short breaks where it's not quite as heavy.

He charged me eighty bucks just to look at it for five minutes. He had this really elaborate tool belt, though, made of real leather. It squeaked every time he shifted his weight. My uncle used to make leather belts by hand. He had this whole workshop in his garage that smelled like dye and sawdust. I tried to help him once when I was a kid, but I accidentally knocked over a jar of rivets. They went everywhere, and it took us an hour to sweep them all up. We found them under the workbench for years after that. 

But yeah, I don't know what else to tell you about the depression part. Like I said, it's just been there pretty much all day, every day, for a really long time.

Mud is so weird, isn't it? It's just dirt and water, but it can completely ruin your car mats. But yeah, no, I haven't been having thoughts about death or anything like that. Just feeling really weighed down.

I ended up folding it up and putting it in my closet next to my winter coats. I have this one coat that I got at a thrift store years ago. It's real wool, super heavy, and it smells faintly like mothballs no matter how many times I get it dry cleaned. The dry cleaner near my apartment is run by this older couple who always argue about the television volume while they're ringing me up. They have this tiny little TV mounted in the corner that's always playing daytime soap operas. I don't get how people can watch those shows, the acting is always so dramatic. 

But yeah, anyway, those symptoms you mentioned—the low mood, the sleep stuff, the guilt, not wanting to do anything—they've been hanging around pretty much the whole time, day in and day out.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of persistent depression, loss of interest in activities, changes in appetite, sleep disturbances, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, and diminished ability to think or concentrate are consistent with a diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder, Unspecified.
